hints: Look closely at the functional groups sticking out from the rings, what atoms do you see that are perfect for hydrogen bonding?
Count the many -OH groups on this cellulose chain, they can donate and accept hydrogen bonds both with neighbouring chains and with water.
Think about burning separately from gentle oxidation, does being a secondary alcohol stop a carbohydrate-rich material like cardboard from combusting?
walkthrough:
**Recognise the polymer as cellulose**

This is part of cellulose, the natural polysaccharide in cardboard and paper. Notice the glucose rings linked by ether (glycosidic) links.

Key groups present: $\text{-OH}$ and $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ on every unit

**Check statement 1 - hydrogen bonding between chains**

Hydrogen bonding needs H attached to O, N or F, plus a lone pair on O, N or F. Each $\text{-OH}$ group can both donate and accept.

$$\text{R-O-H} \cdots \text{O-R}$$ 
So neighbouring cellulose chains form extensive hydrogen bonds with each other. Statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2 - interaction with water**

Water, $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, also forms hydrogen bonds. The $\text{-OH}$ groups on the polymer can hydrogen bond to water molecules.

$$\text{R-O-H} \cdots \text{O-H}_2$$
This is why paper absorbs water and goes soggy. Statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3 - burning and alcohol type**

Combustion is complete oxidation to $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and all alcohols, primary, secondary or tertiary, burn easily in oxygen. Secondary only matters for mild oxidation with acidified dichromate to a ketone.

$$\text{carbohydrate + O}_2 \rightarrow \text{CO}_2 + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
Cardboard burns very easily. Statement 3 is incorrect, so only 1 and 2 are correct.

options.A: This option claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 1 and 2 are true due to the many -OH groups, but 3 is false because all alcohols burn readily and cardboard is very flammable.
options.B: This option states only 1 and 2 are correct. This is right because the -OH groups allow hydrogen bonding between polymer chains and with water, while statement 3 confuses combustion with mild oxidation.
options.C: This option claims 2 and 3 are correct but omits 1. Statement 1 is definitely correct as -OH to -OH hydrogen bonding holds cellulose chains together, and statement 3 is false.
options.D: This option claims only 1 is correct. Statement 2 is also correct because the same -OH groups that bond chain to chain can also hydrogen bond to water molecules, which is why cardboard absorbs water.
